subject: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-099.turn3.draft.md
summary: Turn 3 lands the unique current-cycle pin table, dedicated stopped-after-exec launches, Linux target auxv ABI source, and macOS target P_TRANSLATED source. It also preserves the five D-006 startup gates, the weekly-roll 10% rule, all numeric threshold numerals, condition 5, and the implementation freeze. The macOS preflight is nevertheless not executable as written: PROC_PIDT_SHORTBSDINFO returns a structure with no start-time fields, and KERN_PROC_PID returns kinfo_proc with no CPU-type field. Because unreadable fields invalidate a job, both macOS classes would reject every sample; substituting executable file metadata would recreate the process-architecture defect. This MUST-FIX prohibits CONSENT and the proposed condition-4 MET transition.

objections.title: The macOS 15 preflight requests start-time and CPU-type fields that its named structures do not contain
objections.finding: Lines 214-215 say proc_pidinfo(T, PROC_PIDT_SHORTBSDINFO) supplies start tv_sec/tv_usec. On the target macOS 15.4 SDK, that flavor returns struct proc_bsdshortinfo, which has no start-time members; pbi_start_tvsec and pbi_start_tvusec belong to struct proc_bsdinfo returned by PROC_PIDTBSDINFO. Lines 216-220 then say sysctl(CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID, T) returns a kinfo_proc CPU type. kinfo_proc embeds struct extern_proc, which has p_flag (and therefore the correctly named P_TRANSLATED bit) but no CPU-type member. The target SDK also has no PROC_PIDARCHINFO or struct proc_archinfo that could silently supply the missing process field. A syntax-only probe against MacOSX15.4.sdk fails exactly on proc_bsdshortinfo.pbi_start_tvsec, proc_bsdshortinfo.pbi_start_tvusec, and kinfo_proc.kp_proc.p_cputype.
evidence: D-099 turn 3 lines 214-220 name PROC_PIDT_SHORTBSDINFO start fields and a kinfo_proc CPU-type field.

/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX15.4.sdk/usr/include/sys/proc_info.h defines pbi_start_tvsec/pbi_start_tvusec only on struct proc_bsdinfo, defines struct proc_bsdshortinfo without them, and binds PROC_PIDT_SHORTBSDINFO to sizeof(struct proc_bsdshortinfo). Its SHA-256 is 9548e28972bd1653a6adb673d17beb975ae26a79e673a697434945bcb79d4059.

/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX15.4.sdk/usr/include/sys/sysctl.h defines kinfo_proc as extern_proc plus eproc; /usr/include/sys/proc.h defines extern_proc without a CPU-type field and defines P_TRANSLATED in p_flag. Their SHA-256 values are 32d463b3d01a2999b10865cc4e032a8b5959ab8d2b5e0c71ce820fe81fe53f82 and ecfcb2d5fdfe030f3b3197d3313b9d13875f1f8a345c6a9c75b7e82dc7052e64.

A clang -fsyntax-only probe against MacOSX15.4.sdk reports: no member named pbi_start_tvsec in struct proc_bsdshortinfo; no member named pbi_start_tvusec in struct proc_bsdshortinfo; no member named p_cputype in struct extern_proc.

The macOS translation half is distinct and valid at the field level: the same target kinfo_proc can expose kp_proc.p_flag & P_TRANSLATED after the suspended spawn. The defect is the separate, nonexistent process-CPU field and the wrong start-info flavor.
objections.impact: The global fail-closed clause makes every macos-15 and macos-15-intel job invalid because two required fields cannot be read from the named results. An implementation that instead treats file/lipo output as the missing process architecture would again observe executable metadata rather than T's selected process ABI. Therefore the proposed G03/G04 harness names are not backed by a runnable four-platform contract, and condition 4 cannot become MET.
objections.requiredRepair: Replace the start-identity step with a real macOS 15 field and flavor, such as PROC_PIDTBSDINFO with struct proc_bsdinfo.pbi_start_tvsec/pbi_start_tvusec or the already obtained kinfo_proc.kp_proc.p_starttime, with exact return-size and error checks. Replace the invented kinfo_proc CPU type with a documented target-PID process-architecture observation actually available on macOS 15, naming its API, returned structure, normalized values, and failure behavior; if no such external field is available, define a reviewed post-exec in-target report or a different reviewed proof rather than falling back to file/lipo. Retain T's post-exec kinfo_proc P_TRANSLATED check and the suspended-spawn handshake. Because this is turn 3 of 3, repair requires the protocol's post-cycle route, not a fourth turn.

notes.title: AT_PLATFORM is a target-memory pointer, not an inline auxv string
notes.finding: The Linux intent is clear enough not to create a second rejecting finding: /proc/T/auxv is target-specific and the accepted values are strings. At implementation time, however, each auxv record contains an ID and machine-word value, and AT_PLATFORM's value is a pointer into T's initial stack. The harness must dereference that pointer through a bounded target-memory read while T is stopped; it must not call getauxval() in the parent or compare the raw address.
notes.routing: Make the dereference, NUL/length bound, target-memory API, and read failure explicit when authoring the harness or in the next reviewed successor.
